_note: Revelation staging — how the Chair chooses to present a Nexus directive to the Board. Doubt is applied PER MEMBER using their credibility profile (board/credibility.json), so the same framing costs different amounts with different people. Doubt drivers per design-document §6: severity of language, consistency with the Chair's established precedent, and frequency.

framings.name: Faithful proclamation
framings._note: Full favour and full effect. The doctrinal members barely blink; Engineering counts the days since the last one.

framings.name: Reinterpreted teaching
framings.description: Softened to fit what the Board already expects to hear.
framings._note: Partial favour, partial effect. Dangerous specifically in front of the Archive rep, who knows the texts better than the Chair does.

framings.name: Buried footnote
framings.description: Slipped in as a minor technical clause nobody reads twice.
framings._note: Nearly free on doubt for most members and actively suspicious to Order, whose religion is procedure. Costs paper, because a footnote has to be written down.

framings.name: Withhold
framings.description: Not brought to the Board at all.
framings._note: No doubt and no compliance. The risk is not the Board — it is the audit. auditRisk is the per-directive chance the Presidium notices, and noticing is what starts the road to the takeover.

doubtModifiers._note: Applied on top of the per-member doubtGain. Consistency is the interesting one: a harsh revelation after a lenient record reads as suspicious, because the text has not changed in decades — so why does its meaning keep shifting to match convenience?
doubtModifiers._frequencyNote: One proclamation a year feels sacred; one a month feels well-timed.
